title: What each one is: MF, PMS, AIF
objectives: Explain mutual funds, PMS and AIFs in plain words, with minimum tickets.
Say what makes an AIF different from a mutual fund.
body_md:
All three are SEBI-regulated professional money management, but a mutual fund is open to everyone, a PMS is a personal portfolio from ₹50 lakh, and an AIF is a privately placed pooled fund, typically from ₹1 crore. Mutual fund (MF): a pooled fund regulated under SEBI's Mutual Fund Regulations. Investors own units; the fund is diversified, highly liquid and tightly regulated on costs and disclosure. Portfolio Management Service (PMS): a portfolio of securities managed for one client, held in that client's own demat account. SEBI minimum ₹50 lakh. Alternative Investment Fund (AIF): a privately pooled fund regulated under SEBI's AIF Regulations, 2012. It can invest in assets mutual funds largely cannot, such as unlisted companies, private credit or real estate. Minimum ₹1 crore per investor (₹25 lakh for the manager's employees and directors), up to 1,000 investors per scheme, sold only by private placement.

> **Talk-track:** “All three are professionally managed and SEBI-regulated. The difference is how much you put in, how long it's locked, what it can invest in, and how it's taxed.”

> **Investor takeaway:** Bigger ticket and more exclusive do not mean better. Each product suits a different investor.
example: ₹500 a month buys a mutual fund SIP; ₹50 lakh is the PMS minimum; ₹1 crore is the AIF minimum for most investors.
say: All three are professionally managed and SEBI-regulated.
The difference is ticket, lock-in, holdings and tax.

check.q: What is the SEBI minimum investment for a PMS?
check.why: ₹50 lakh. The minimum was raised to ₹50 lakh in 2020.

check.q: What is the minimum investment for an AIF for most investors?
check.why: ₹1 crore. ₹25 lakh applies only to the manager's employees and directors.

check.q: How many investors can an AIF scheme have at most?
check.why: 1,000. AIF schemes are capped at 1,000 investors.
